# General Social Survey: agent index

A repeated cross-sectional survey of US adults, 1972 to 2024, about attitudes, behaviors and attributes.

Publisher: NORC at the University of Chicago. Dataset id: `gss`. Records follow PublicDataToolkit standard 0.1.

Terms: https://gss.norc.org/terms-and-conditions.html. LLM processing: `allowed`.

Dimensions: `wave` is the year; `form` is the ballot.

## Releases

| `7224r3a` | - | 6943 | GSS 1972-2024 Cross-Sectional Cumulative Data, Release 3a |
| `7224r3` | - | 6942 | GSS 1972-2024 Cross-Sectional Cumulative Data, Release 3 |

## Corrections applied

These records had an error in the source documentation. The shards show the corrected value; the JSONL `view.corrected` block gives the original, the problem and the confidence.

- `racfew` /questions/0/text (inferred): The question text stops mid-sentence.
- `rachaf` /questions/0/text (verified): A stray space after the hyphen in 'African- Americans'.
- `racopen` /questions/0/text (verified): The text of the two laws is missing, so the codes 'first law' and 'second law' can't be interpreted.
- `racschol` /questions/0/text (verified): The question text belongs to a different item; the value labels ('same schools', 'separate schools') don't match it.
- `racfew` /questions/0/text (inferred): The question text stops mid-sentence.

## How the shards are organized

Every shard is the result of a filter over the records, and its header says which filter and what completeness label it supports. Each shard comes in two forms with the same variables: `.txt`, one line per variable, for scanning; and `.jsonl`, the records with corrections applied, for details. The first JSONL line is the shard's header (`{"shard": ...}`); every later line is a variable. A shard too big to read at once (about 20,000 tokens) is split into parts.

The JSONL records are compact: `availability` maps each form (or `all`) to runs of waves, `origins` gives where each field came from as `kind:source` or `rule:name@version`, and `origins.codes` is the origin the codes share (a code lists its own when they differ). Per-wave counts and the notes on origins are left out. The full records in `metadata/` are canonical; each shard header's `full_records` names the files.

Line form: `name | waves by form | scale signature | label | question text`. A run like `1972-1978` means every wave of the release in that span. `1972-1985,1987-2024 (not 1986)` means the release has a 1986 wave and the variable wasn't in it. `all 1972-1987; form A,C 1988-2024` means everyone was asked through 1987 and only forms A and C from 1988. The release's waves are: `7224r3a`: 1972-1978,1980,1982-1991,1993-1994,1996,1998,2000,2002,2004,2006,2008,2010,2012,2014,2016,2018,2021-2022,2024; `7224r3`: 1972-1978,1980,1982-1991,1993-1994,1996,1998,2000,2002,2004,2006,2008,2010,2012,2014,2016,2018,2021-2022,2024. A trailing `*` on a name means a field was corrected.

`SKILL.md` says how to label an answer drawn from these files.
